locator: Lifetime Drug Abuse/Dependence and Lifetime Alcohol Dependence (p.429); Family, Social, and Individual Factors (p.429); Comment, second paragraph beginning p.431 and continuing p.432
extracted: Drug abuse/dependence questions were asked for drug classes used at least monthly. Abuse used either of two symptoms and dependence two or more of four symptoms; the authors state these are not formal DSM-IV criteria. Alcohol dependence used full DSM-IV criteria. The authors acknowledge no ages at progression to frequent use or onset of problems, so lifetime drug-problem or alcohol-dependence comparisons do not establish that problems began after early cannabis initiation. The listed within-pair covariates include psychiatric disorders, social anxiety, early tobacco use and early regular drinking; peer affiliation and temperament are not described as measured covariates (editors’ reading of the described assessment, not a claim that the broader registry never measured them). Separate identical/fraternal analyses are described as confirming conclusions without printed estimates.
